messages:
ryan: quick brain dump — thinking about a cooperative allocator handoff to reduce fragmentation spikes when we offload pages from GPU -> host. idea: CPU side can pre-reserve "shadow" regions that mirror GPU allocations and we do a soft handoff notification instead of immediate migration. keeps GPU pointers stable and gives CPU allocator time to coalesce without blocking inference.
anya: can you sketch the race you're worried about? e.g., gpu evicts, cpu reuses, gpu still holds kv cache ptrs?
kai: yeah race is real. one option is to use a small generation counter per logical allocation + ephemeral handles. GPU KV cache stores handle, not raw host ptr. on handoff we bump gen so stale handles fail fast. pseudo: ```handle = alloc_logical(size); ptr = resolve(handle, gen); // kernel maps when pinned```
anya: switching to handles sounds invasive for runtime. how do we do this without touching model runtime ABI?
ryan: two phased approach: (1) short term: shadow reservations + conservative reuse delays (configurable ms); GPU keeps raw ptrs during delay. (2) long term: logical residency layer that exposes handles; runtimes opt-in.
lina: perf concern — extra indirection or resolve calls per token could be bad. have we measured cost? even a few hundred ns hurts at low-latency SLOs.
daniel: agree — need microbenchmarks. propose experiments: a) `resolve()` nop cost, b) resolve + cache-miss path, c) handoff delay windows 5/10/50ms. collect p50/p95/p99 latency, eviction-rate, fragmentation-ratio.
ryan: good. metrics we should add: `redwood_mem_fragmentation_ratio`, `handoff_failures_total`, `logical_resolve_ns_p50/p99`. add them to console dashboards for the canary.
infra-bot: deploy scheduled: alloc-proto-experiments -> canary us-west-2 at 2026-03-23T02:00:00Z :rocket:
kai: alternative less-invasive option: use a freelist quarantine like jemalloc's tcache but at host staging pool level. i.e., when we evict from GPU, put pages into a short quarantine (e.g., 30-100ms) before returning to general pool. reduces reuse races and fragmentation without ABI changes.
lina: quarantine seems simple and lower-risk. question: how do we size quarantine per-device to avoid running out of host ram? need admission control and backpressure to GPU evictor.
ryan: yep admission control required. propose per-GPU soft quota: `quarantine_limit_bytes` and `quarantine_high_water_ms`. if quota exceeded we start synchronous drop/fallback (move to slower-tier disk-backed staging).
daniel: for experiments, we should simulate high-alloc churn with realistic seq-length distributions. i can wire up the harness from `perf/harness/evict_sim` and add flags for quarantine sizes.
anya: billing/accounting note — if quarantined pages stay on host longer we may need to reflect that in tenant memory metrics to avoid overcharging surprises. liaise with finance for visible metering.
ryan: ack — I'll include a short section in RFC about accounting. i'll draft RFC w/ diagrams: quarantine vs handles vs soft handoff. aim to post by Friday. @kai can you prototype the quarantine implementation? @lina can you set a perf budget for p99 penalties we can accept?
kai: on it. will mock the freelist and add metrics.
lina: will work on perf targets and write the dashboard queries.
ryan: thanks all — short-term plan: quarantine with admission control + canary. long-term: logical residency/handle layer. i'll drop a link to the RFC draft once ready. :+1:
